(a) Use \[\begin{gathered}f(x) \\ =(x^2+x-1)(4x^2+x+4) \\ +kx +k -5\end{gathered}\]. At \(x=-2\), \(0=18-k-5\), giving \(k=13\).
(b) Substitute \(-\frac14\) into this identity to get \(f(-\frac14)=0\).
(c) The two known roots give factors \(x+2\) and \(4x+1\). Dividing the expanded polynomial \[\begin{gathered}4x^4 +5x^3 +x^2 \\ +16x +4\end{gathered}\] by these factors gives \(x^2-x+2\). Hence \[\begin{gathered}f(x) \\ =(x+2)(4x+1)(x^2-x+2)\end{gathered}\]. The last factor has discriminant \(-7\), so has no real linear factors.
